 3m ago 11.29 EDT Liverpool push for a third goal, Gakpo away down the right but failing to find the ma in the middle.
 Share 5m ago 11.27 EDT United are, at least, spending some time attacking this half, Martinez shooting wide from distance, but they’re not sustaining attacks not seriously extending Petrovic. At Anfield, Nyoni has replaced Wirtz but is now struggling himself.
 Share 7m ago 11.26 EDT Another change from Carrick and again it’s not Bruno, Martinez on for Heaven, who had a shocker. For all the difference it makes, Rayan easing past Dalot and running atMartinez, who steps across him, only to allow his man through on the inside. he has options at the far post too, but opts to shoot, his low effort scuttling just wide.
 Share 9m ago 11.24 EDT GOAL! Hull City 1-1 Brentford (Ouattara 63)
 A ball swung into the box bumps about, then Igor Thiago finds Ouattara and he taps home from a few yards.
 View image in fullscreen Dango Ouattara equalises for Brentford! Photograph: Alex Livesey/Getty Images Share Updated at  11.29 EDT 11m ago 11.21 EDT Change for Bournemouth, Gannon-Doak on for Kluivert.
 Share 12m ago 11.21 EDT United are pushing at OT, Mbeumo going down when Adams jumps into him – United want a penalty but they’re never getting that – then, when Yoro finds him, he swings a shot over the bar. So they come again, Dalot lifting over Smith’s foot to go down the line and winning a corner, driven into Petrovic’s gloves.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Share Updated at  11.25 EDT 13m ago 11.19 EDT At Anfield, Brighton probe seeking a route back into the game, Yalcouye on for Chema. Oh, and as I type, Wirtz flails a leg at Ayari, fouling with the ball out of reach, lands awkwardly, and gosh, he looks in a lot of pain. He does, though, make a quick recovery, so will, I think, be back on shortly.
 Share 16m ago 11.16 EDT GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-2 Newcastle United (Barnes 58)
 Pierre Sage is another manager in deep trouble, Newcastle working Dedic into space down the right of the box, with his hard square-pass swept home by Barnes.
 View image in fullscreen Harvey Barnes makes it 2-0 to Newcastle. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at  11.21 EDT 17m ago 11.15 EDT In comms, Gary Neville thinks Tielemans should’ve stayed on with Andrey Santos going off, and it’s hard to argue with that. United need goals, Tielemans can supply them, and Baleba should supply the solidity necessary given the game-state.
 Share 19m ago 11.14 EDT “Half-time sacking,” begins Ingo hHrtzke. “That question has come up before – so I’m once more sending a famous example from Germany’s 2nd division, about 26 years ago in December 1999 Toni Schumacher was managing Fortuna Cologne, who had a very colourful chairman at the time: Jean Löring. After a spell of bad results they were trailing 0-2 at home to Mannheim at half time, Löring stormed into the dressing room and shouted: ‘Piss off, you wanker! I never want to see you again.’ (That’s how Schumacher told it in his memoir.) To the press afterwards, he spoke the immortal words: ‘As the club, I had to act.’ Classic.”
 A lovely example of l’etat c’est moi, but looking at this United side, 1999 was at least 260 years ago.
 Share 21m ago 11.11 EDT I’m not sure what Carrick’s trying to achieve by not bringing Bruno on. United probably won’t come back with him, but without him, it feels impossible.
 Share 22m ago 11.10 EDT At Palace, Willock is sent through and finishes well, doing what Rayan tried to but well … only for VAR to show a shoulder offside.
 Share 23m ago 11.10 EDT Heaven, having a mare, passes straight to Rayan, who exchanges passes with Kluivert then opens body to find the far corner only to finish too close to Lammens, who saves.
 Share 24m ago 11.08 EDT Not all that long ago, in October 2018, Jose Mourinho was about to get sacked with United 2-o down at home to Newcastle. Then they came back, won 3-2, and Mourinho lasted until just before Christmas, wreaking yet further havoc in the meantime.
 Share 26m ago 11.07 EDT Goodness me, a ricochet off heaven, dithering from Maguire, and a pass in behind is tucked away by Evanilson … who’s offside. He leaves that for Rayan, and it’s 3-0. United are an absolute debacle.
 Share 27m ago 11.05 EDT GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-1 Newcastle United (Osula 48)
 Newcastle build down the right and Murphy swings over a brilliant cross, which Osula tucks home at the near post and on the volley.
 View image in fullscreen Will Osula scores for Newcastle! Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian View image in fullscreen Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at  11.13 EDT 29m ago 11.04 EDT At Old Trafford, still no Bruno Fernandes, but Cunha is on for Tielemans. We’re underway again.
 Share 30m ago 11.03 EDT “Eamon Dunphy, in his fine diary of a season Only a Game?, broke the substitute’s omertà by revealing that most players who are dropped are delighted when their replacements fail on the pitch,” says Justin Kavanagh. “I’m sure Bruno Fernandes has a warm glow inside as he sits listening to Carrick’s half-time farewell speech team-talk.”
 I found that book in the school library aged about 13 and it properly opened my eyes. I was lucky enough to interview Dunphy when making the film Busby, a complete thrill – his book A Strange Kind of Glory is a classic – and only he would have tossed all the interviews he did for it.
 Share 34m ago 10.58 EDT Half-time email: “Isak, Wirtz and Barcola seem to be finding their feet at last,” writes Colum Fordham, “and pretty good feet they have too. Liverpool once again pose an attacking threat to any team but the shambolic defence – Van Dijk a shadow of his former self and the erratic Kerkez - threaten to undo the good work. Araujo is definitely one of the most exciting of the new acquisitions for the Reds, his dynamism and strength very much needed. Iraola is managing to keep the dangerous Brighton at bay.”
 I’m still not convinced by Wirtz, who flits in and out and doesn’t, I don’t think, make good decisions quickly enough when nuder pressure. But Isak is a class act, and Barcola is excellent when offered space in behind. I don’t love him in tight situations, but if he can improve his, er key actions , i.e. his final pass and finishing, he can be a factor in the Prem.
 Share 37m ago 10.56 EDT Looking again at the second Bournemouth goal, Yoro, though he slips, also slows down, when all he needed to do was tap back to Lammens. Without that indecision, he’s no chance to slip because the ball’s already gone.
 Share 38m ago 10.55 EDT I’d not be shocked if Carrick makes United’s call for them, Kevin Keegan for England-style – or wouldn’t be if there wasn’t cashmoney involved. He surely knows this is too far gone for him to resolve, and he’s clearly hating every second of it.
 Share 39m ago 10.53 EDT Scottish Premiership: Durán caps Celtic’s comeback win over Hibernian Read more Share 40m ago 10.53 EDT Also going on: 
 England all out for 241 against Pakistan despite Duckett’s 105: tri-series one day international cricket – live Read more Share 41m ago 10.52 EDT HALF-TIME: Hull City 1-0 Brentford
 McBurnie’s penalty the difference at the KC as Hull continue their fine start to Premier League life.
 Share 41m ago 10.51 EDT HALF-TIME: Manchester United 0-2 AFC Bournemouth
 Bournemouth have been energetically excellent, United soporifically shambolic.
 Share 43m ago 10.49 EDT HALF-TIME: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton & Hove Albion
 Liverpool look really good going forward but so do Brighton; neither look much cop at the back.
 Share 44m ago 10.49 EDT United make a bit of space and Tielemans squares for Santos, who near-enough misses his kick, then the ref goes to book Maguire for a shove earlier in the piece.
 Share 45m ago 10.48 EDT HALF-TIME: Crystal Palace 0-0 Newcastle United
 Nothing between the teams at Selhurst.
 View image in fullscreen It’s Nothing-Nil in south London. Photograph: Javier García/Shutterstock Share Updated at  10.59 EDT 45m ago 10.47 EDT Two additional minutes at Old Trafford, three at Anfield. Meantime, Amad chops inside Smith and falls – he wants a penalty, but it’s nothing of the sort.
 Share 46m ago 10.46 EDT “This must be the most mediocre Man Utd XI since the late 80s side of Duxbury, Phelan and Blackmore,” writes Brian Broderick. “But if you give Chelsea £100m for Mount and Santos, that’s where you end up. Which is pretty much what Martinez was saying.”
 At least those United sides had Robson, Hughes, Whiteside and McGrath, absolute giants all. I said earlier there are some good players in this squad and there are, but they’re devoid of confidence, organisation and moxie.
 Share 48m ago 10.45 EDT GOAL! Manchester United 0-2 AFC Bournemouth (Tavernier 41)
 Has a manager ever been sacked at half-time before? A ball in behind Yoro should pose no problem but, out of nowhere but also straight out of M16, Yoro slips, Truffert squares, and Tavernier sweeps home. United are awful, while Bournemouth are all over it.
 View image in fullscreen Uh oh. Marcus Tavernier makes it 2-0. Photograph: Conor Molloy/ProSports/Shutterstock Share Updated at  10.48 EDT 50m ago 10.43 EDT United try to hit back immediately. First, Tielemans is booked, then Mount, having wandered infield, slides a pass ahead of Mbeumo, inside-left position, and he shoots across goal, but Petrovic tips away. “Down with the City!” choruses the away end.
 Share 51m ago 10.41 EDT GOAL! Manchester United 0-1 AFC Bournemouth (Rayan 38)
 Loads of players stand offside and come back but Rayan, the furthest left, is alone and on, mooching on to Kluivert’s outswinging cross to guide a sidefooter into the ground and past Lammens at his near post. It’s been coming.
 View image in fullscreen Oh dear. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters View image in fullscreen Rayan scores for Bournemouth! Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.47 EDT 53m ago 10.39 EDT Back to Old Trafford now, where Heaven launches two-footed into a challenge, and is saved by Evanilson stepping out of the way. He’s booked, but if he’d made contact, it’s a red card; lucky boy.
 Share 54m ago 10.38 EDT A poor kick-out from Alisson puts Liverpool in trouble and Brighton win the ball back, working it to Ayari, who bends a low shot around the keeper, not yet back on his line … and hits the base of the post!
 Share 1h ago 10.37 EDT Harry Messguire lummoxes past a few challenges, but can’t find a shooting lane, so passes backwards The crowd though, appreciate the intention and might it spur United to do something? They get the ball wide to Amad, who then leaves it behind him and, when he gets it back, plays a poor pass.
 Share 1h ago 10.36 EDT “The Seagulls have been a shambles at the back,” reckons Kári Tulinius. “Being 2-0 down is the least they deserve. Nevertheless, when they mount an attack, Liverpool defend in a panic, and I doubt they’ll keep a clean sheet. There’s no way there won’t be more goals in this match.”
 I ‘m inclined to agree – Brighton attack well and Liverpool defend chaotically. If the former manage a livener before the latter bag a clincher, this could be a really exciting contest.
 Share 1h ago 10.34 EDT United are offering so little in attack – no width, no 1v1 ability, no sharp passing – and when, as I type, a lovely flick behind the standing leg allows Baleba to find Tielemans, Mbeumo checks his run and the attempted through-pass is easily cut out.
 Share 1h ago 10.32 EDT Better from United, Yoro into Tielemans, who flicks superbly for Baleba down the right. He’s got Mbeumo in the middle, but roughly 94 defenders blocking the route to him, and Hill does well to slide in and intercept the cross.
 Share 1h ago 10.30 EDT A decent ball in from Adams, to which an unsighted Evanilson can’t quite introduce a head. Bournemouth haven’t had that many chances, but they’ve had loads of good situations, whereas United have had none.
 Share 1h ago 10.29 EDT GOAL! Hull City 1-0 Brentford (McBurnie 24 pen)
 We’re not shown for what it was given, but McBurnie dispatches it with a confident roll, Kelleher diving out of the road.
 View image in fullscreen Oli McBurnie puts Hull ahead from the spot. Photograph: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock Share Updated at  10.33 EDT 1h ago 10.28 EDT United are just so careless with the ball. Lammens catches a cross and tries to set a counter in motion, but his roll-out sells Mbeumo short and instead, Bournemouth counter. Oh and Andre Santos was booked a few minutes for a lunge; the same has since been done by and to Tyler Adams.
 Share 1h ago 10.26 EDT It didn’t look great initially ad they’re still too easy to get at, but we can now say that Liverpool have made a decent start under Andoni Iraola. They’ve got into the habit of winning, Isak is scoring, and they’ve loads of attacking options, while Araujo has given them physicality and aggression they lacked not just last season but even the one before when they won the league.
 Share 1h ago 10.23 EDT GOAL! Liverpool 2-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Isak 21)
 It’s taken a while, but Alexander Isak is a Liverpool player now. Boscagli makes a mess controlling an Alisson kick, Barcola does really well to rob him, and from there, it’s simple competence, a careful cross into the middle and a composed sidefooted finish. Yasiin Ayari will be feeling very, very poorly, and this could yet get a lot worse.
 View image in fullscreen Alexander Isak makes it 2-0 to Liverpool. What a start for the home side! Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.26 EDT 1h ago 10.21 EDT Liverpool keep at it, Verbruggen forced to dive full-length to stop a shot directed across him by Gakpo. Meantime, back in Manchester, it’s now a more even game, though Boournemouth know they can pretty much allow Dalot to have the ball in dangerous areas because nothing will happen thereafter – and, as I type, he lashes a hopeful shot miles from anywhere.
 Share 1h ago 10.19 EDT GOAL! Liverpool 1-0 Brighton & Hove Albion (Wirtz 17)
 That is how much Brighton will regret missing that chance. Araujo does brilliantly down the right – what an acquisition he’s been so far – ruckusing hard to recover possession before crossing low. The ball hits Gross, lands in front of Wirtz, and though he shoots seeking the far corner, a huge deflection off Andres wrongfoots Verbruggen and gives Liverpool the lead.
 View image in fullscreen Florian Wirtz fires Liverpool in front! Photograph: Jan Kruger/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.22 EDT 1h ago 10.17 EDT Back to OT and it’s slightly better from United, Mbeumo finding space before running into trouble. They are, though, keeping the ball now, with Baleba seemingly settled into the game.
 Share 1h ago 10.16 EDT Oh, but here come Brighton! They fight down the right, Gomez in behind and taking a pass from Gross before cutting back for Ayari, 10 yards out … who panels over the bar! What a chance that was, and how might Brighton rue spurning it?
 Share 1h ago 10.14 EDT At Anfield, Costinha has replaced Kadioglu, who gives Brighton so much attacking impetus. We’ve barely seen them in the Liverpool half yet, but they’ve done well to survive the opening period … as have United, sort of – so far, their performance is such that to say they’ve done anything well feels ridiculous. And, as I type, a flick off Yoro prevents a cross from arriving at Evanilson.
